title: Run for shelter to the Lord of daybreak.
subtitle: The One who splits the night with morning
then: Ibn Abbas and many others said {idea}Al-Falaq is the morning{/idea}, like the verse: He is the Cleaver of the daybreak. The Prophet ﷺ said of this surah and the next: {reward}people do not seek protection with anything like these two{/reward}. He told Uqbah to recite them on sleeping and waking.
now: 3 a.m., awake with worry. The room is dark, every fear is louder. You know the dawn will come in a few hours. {idea}You turn to the One who brings it.{/idea} He breaks the night every single day; He can break yours.
old: When I am afraid, I have to find my own way out.
new: The Lord who splits the night every morning is the One I run to when afraid.
try: Recite Al-Falaq and An-Nas before sleeping tonight and when you wake tomorrow.

title: From the harm of everything He created.
subtitle: One refuge covers all harm
then: Ibn Kathir says this means {trap}from the evil of all created things{/trap}. Thabit Al-Bunani and Al-Hasan gave examples: Hell, and Iblis and his offspring, {idea}among what He created{/idea}. Every harm is a creation, and its Creator holds it.
now: Viruses, car crashes, scams, bad people, your own temper. You cannot guard against everything. {idea}One sentence covers it all{/idea}, because all of it belongs to the One you are asking.
old: There are too many dangers to protect myself from.
new: Every danger is something Allah created. I seek refuge with its Creator.
try: Before leaving home today, recite this surah and trust the day to Allah.

title: From the harm of the night when it settles.
subtitle: When darkness spreads

row.title: the moon
sub: the Prophet ﷺ pointed to it

then: Mujahid and many others said ghasiq is {idea}the night when it advances with its darkness{/idea}. A'ishah said the Prophet ﷺ took her hand, showed her the rising moon, and said: {reward}seek refuge with Allah from the evil of this ghasiq when it darkens{/reward}.
now: Nights are when the bad habits come out: the late scrolling, the lonely spiral, the arguments that should have waited for morning. {idea}Darkness gives cover to harm, inside and out.{/idea} The verse hands you something to say as the sun goes down.
old: Night is just the time between days.
new: Night brings its own harms. I enter it with Allah's protection.
try: When you see the moon tonight, seek refuge with Allah from its night, as the Prophet ﷺ taught.

title: From the harm of those who blow on knots.
subtitle: Protection from magic, without obsession
then: Mujahid and others said this means {trap}those who practise magic and blow into knots{/trap}. When the Prophet ﷺ was affected and then cured, A'ishah asked if he would make it public. He said: {reward}Allah has cured me, and I hate to stir up evil among people{/reward}.
now: Some people see magic behind every bad day and every illness, and start suspecting relatives. The Prophet ﷺ, when it truly happened to him, {idea}sought refuge, was cured, and refused to spread blame{/idea}. Protect yourself with these words, and then leave suspicion alone.
old: If something goes wrong, someone must have done something to me.
new: I seek refuge in Allah from real harm, and I do not go looking for people to blame.
try: Instead of suspecting anyone, recite the last three surahs over yourself today and trust Allah.

title: From the harm of the envier when he envies.
subtitle: Envy turns harmful when acted on
then: The surah ends with envy. Jibril recited a ruqyah over the Prophet ﷺ: {reward}in the name of Allah, from every illness, from the evil of every envier and evil eye{/reward}. The verse says {trap}when he envies{/trap}: the harm is in envy acted upon.
now: You post the new job and feel a cold reply from a friend. Or you see a cousin's wedding photos and feel something tighten in your own chest. {idea}Seek refuge from the envier, and from becoming one.{/idea} Saying masha'Allah is the cure for your side.
old: Envy is something other people feel toward me.
new: I seek protection from others' envy and guard my own heart from it too.
try: When you see someone's blessing today, say masha'Allah, barakallahu lak, and mean it.
